question: The monolithic Kailasa Temple at Ellora, carved out of a single rock from top to bottom, was built under the patronage of which dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Rashtrakutas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kailasa (Kailasanatha) Temple, Cave 16 at Ellora, was built in the 8th century CE under the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I. (कैलाश मंदिर, एलोरा — राष्ट्रकूट वंश)

 

• It is the largest monolithic rock-cut structure in the world. Unlike ordinary caves that are tunnelled horizontally into a cliff, Kailasa was carved vertically downwards from the top of the basalt hill, so the entire temple — vimana, mandapa, gateway, Nandi shrine and elephant figures — is a single continuous piece of rock.

 

• The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is designed to represent Mount Kailasa, his mythical abode.

 

• The Ellora caves in Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) district of Maharashtra comprise 34 caves — Buddhist (Caves 1-12), Hindu (Caves 13-29) and Jain (Caves 30-34) — and are a rare example of religious harmony at one site. Ellora was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ellora's Dashavatara Cave (Cave 15) and Vishvakarma Cave (Cave 10, the "carpenter's cave") are also well known; Cave 10 is the only chaitya hall at Ellora.

 

• Ajanta (Buddhist, paintings) and Ellora (three faiths, sculpture) were both inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1983. The Elephanta Caves, near Mumbai, are chiefly Shaivite and famous for the Trimurti sculpture; they were inscribed in 1987.

 

NOTE

 

• The Chalukyas of Badami (Option 2): They excavated the rock-cut cave temples at Badami and built the temple complex at Pattadakal and Aihole in Karnataka.

 

• The Pallavas (Option 3): They built the rathas (monolithic temples) and the Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram, Tamil Nadu.

 

• The Vakatakas (Option 4): Many of the later Ajanta caves and paintings were executed under Vakataka patronage, notably during the reign of Harishena.

question:
Read the following statements about the Hornbill Festival:

1. It is celebrated every year in the first ten days of December.

2. It is held at the Naga Heritage Village, Kisama, near Kohima.

3. It is popularly called the "Festival of Festivals".

Which of the above statements are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3 are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All three statements are correct. The Hornbill Festival is the flagship cultural festival of Nagaland. (हॉर्नबिल महोत्सव — नागालैंड)

 

• Statement 1 is correct: The festival is organised every year from 1 to 10 December, and is timed to coincide with Nagaland's Statehood Day on 1 December (Nagaland became the 16th State of India in 1963).

 

• Statement 2 is correct: It is held at the Naga Heritage Village, Kisama, about 12 km from the state capital Kohima. The name "Kisama" is derived from the two villages Kigwema and Phesama.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: Because it brings together all the major tribes of Nagaland — each of which has its own festivals — on a single platform, it is called the "Festival of Festivals". It was first organised in the year 2000 by the Government of Nagaland.

 

• The festival is named after the hornbill, a large bird that appears repeatedly in the folklore, songs and headgear of almost every Naga tribe.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important festivals of Nagaland include Sekrenyi (Angami tribe), Moatsu and Aoleang (Ao and Konyak tribes), and Tuluni (Sumi tribe).

 

• Nagaland shares its borders with Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and the country of Myanmar. Its official language is English.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 are incorrect because each of them leaves out one statement that is factually accurate.

question:
Fill in the blanks:

In Hindustani classical music, the rhythmic cycle of 16 matras divided into four equal vibhags of four beats each is known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Teentaal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Teentaal (Trital) is the most widely used taal in Hindustani classical music. It has 16 matras (beats) arranged in 4 vibhags (sections) of 4 beats each. (तीनताल — 16 मात्रा)

 

• Its structure is marked as X 2 0 3, that is, the first beat is the sam (X), the 5th and 13th beats are tali (clap), and the 9th beat is the khali (wave of the hand).

 

• The bols of Teentaal are: Dha Dhin Dhin Dha | Dha Dhin Dhin Dha | Dha Tin Tin Ta | Ta Dhin Dhin Dha.

 

• In Hindustani music, rhythm is organised as taal, the beat is a matra, a section is a vibhag, the first beat of the cycle is the sam, and the empty beat is the khali.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hindustani music is one of the two main streams of Indian classical music, the other being Carnatic music of South India. In Carnatic music the rhythmic cycle is called tala, the melodic framework raga, and the principal percussion instrument is the mridangam.

 

• Major gharanas of Hindustani vocal music include Gwalior (regarded as the oldest), Agra, Kirana, Jaipur-Atrauli and Patiala.

 

NOTE

 

• Jhaptaal (Option 1): Has 10 matras, divided as 2+3+2+3.

 

• Ektaal (Option 2): Has 12 matras, divided into six vibhags of two beats each; commonly used in vilambit (slow) khayal.

 

• Dadra (Option 4): Has 6 matras, divided into two vibhags of three beats each; widely used in light classical and semi-classical forms.

question: Which of the following statements about the game of Kabaddi is correct?
option_1: Kabaddi was showcased as a demonstration sport at the 1936 Berlin Olympic Games.
option_2: Kabaddi became a medal event at the Asian Games for the first time in 1982.
option_3: The Pro Kabaddi League was launched in India in the year 2010.
option_4: A standard Kabaddi team has nine players on the mat at a time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kabaddi was showcased as a demonstration sport at the 1936 Berlin Olympic Games.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kabaddi was introduced to an international audience when it was demonstrated at the 1936 Berlin Olympics by the Hanuman Vyayam Prasarak Mandal of Amravati, Maharashtra. (कबड्डी — 1936 बर्लिन ओलंपिक)

 

• Kabaddi is the state game of Tamil Nadu, and is also known by regional names such as Hu-Tu-Tu in Maharashtra, Ha-Do-Do in Bengal, Chedugudu in Andhra Pradesh and Sadugudu in Tamil Nadu.

 

• The Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI) was formed in 1973. The game's international body is the International Kabaddi Federation (IKF).

 

• A Kabaddi team has 7 players on the mat (with 5 substitutes). A standard men's match consists of two halves of 20 minutes each with a 5-minute interval, played on a court of 13 m x 10 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first Kabaddi World Cup was held in 2004 and was won by India.

 

• Common Kabaddi terms include raid, raider, antis, lona (bonus for taking all opponents out), do-or-die raid and bonus line.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Kabaddi was a demonstration event at the 1982 Asian Games in New Delhi; it became a medal sport at the 1990 Beijing Asian Games, where India won the gold.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: The Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) was launched in 2014; the inaugural season was won by the Jaipur Pink Panthers.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: A Kabaddi team fields 7 players, not nine. Nine players per side is the format of Kho-Kho.

question: Under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, which body has been created as the principal regulator empowered to grant recognition to National Sports Federations?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The National Sports Board.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Sports Governance Act, 2025 received the assent of President Droupadi Murmu on 18 August 2025. It is the first comprehensive law regulating the administration of sports bodies in India. (राष्ट्रीय खेल अभिशासन अधिनियम, 2025)

 

• The Act sets up the National Sports Board (NSB) as the principal regulatory authority. Its functions include granting recognition to National Sports Federations (NSFs) — which is a precondition for government funding — monitoring their finances, and taking action against irregularities.

 

• The Act also establishes a National Sports Tribunal (NST) for the speedy resolution of sports disputes such as selection disputes, election challenges and disciplinary matters, thereby reducing litigation in civil courts.

 

• Other key features: an Executive Committee of a sports body is capped at 15 members and must include at least two sportspersons of outstanding merit, and the Act aligns Indian sports administration with the Olympic Charter and the Paralympic Charter.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Anti-Doping Act, 2022 created the statutory National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) and the National Dope Testing Laboratory.

 

• Khelo India (launched 2018) and the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) are the two flagship talent-development programmes of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

 

NOTE

 

• The Sports Authority of India (Option 1): Set up in 1984 after the 1982 Asian Games; it is an implementing body for sports promotion and training, not the statutory regulator of federations.

 

• The National Anti-Doping Agency (Option 2): Deals only with anti-doping rules and testing.

 

• The Indian Olympic Association (Option 3): Founded in 1927, it is the National Olympic Committee that selects and sends Indian contingents to the Olympic and Asian Games; it is itself subject to the Act.

question: India's Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA), notable for containing a binding investment and job-creation commitment from the partner side, was signed with which grouping?
option_2: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)
solution_text:
The correct answer is The European Free Trade Association (EFTA).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) was signed on 10 March 2024 and came into force on 1 October 2025. (भारत-ईएफटीए व्यापार एवं आर्थिक भागीदारी समझौता)

 

• EFTA has four member states — Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein. It is not part of the European Union.

 

• TEPA is the first trade agreement in which a partner has given a legally framed investment commitment: EFTA has undertaken to promote USD 100 billion of foreign direct investment in India over 15 years (excluding portfolio investment) and to facilitate the creation of 1 million direct jobs in India.

 

• Switzerland is by far India's largest trading partner within EFTA, largely on account of gold and pharmaceutical trade.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other significant Indian trade pacts: the India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), signed in February 2022 — India's first CEPA with an Arab country; the India-Australia Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (ECTA), 2022; and the India-Mauritius Comprehensive Economic Cooperation and Partnership Agreement (CECPA), India's first trade agreement with an African country.

 

• A Bilateral Investment Treaty (BIT) protects investors of one country in the other, while a CEPA/FTA/TEPA deals mainly with trade in goods and services.

 

NOTE

 

• ASEAN (Option 2): India has the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA), 2009, which is currently under review; ASEAN's Secretariat is in Jakarta.

 

• The GCC (Option 3): India has an FTA with the UAE individually, but a comprehensive India-GCC FTA is still under negotiation.

 

• Mercosur (Option 4): India has only a limited Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) with Mercosur, in force since 2009, covering a small list of products.

question:
Fill in the blanks:

The Santosh Trophy 2024-25 was won by ______, which defeated Kerala 1-0 in the final played at Hyderabad.
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• West Bengal won the Santosh Trophy 2024-25, defeating Kerala 1-0 in the final played at the Gachibowli Stadium, Hyderabad, on 31 December 2024. (संतोष ट्रॉफी — पश्चिम बंगाल)

 

• The winning goal was scored by Robi Hansda in added time; he also finished as the top scorer of the tournament with 12 goals.

 

• This was West Bengal's 33rd Santosh Trophy title, by far the highest by any team, and its first in seven years.

 

• The Santosh Trophy is the National Football Championship for States and Union Territories of India, organised by the All India Football Federation (AIFF). It began in 1941 and is named after the late Maharaja Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhary of Santosh (now in Bangladesh).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The All India Football Federation (AIFF) was founded in 1937 and is headquartered in New Delhi. India's top club competition is the Indian Super League (ISL); the I-League, the Durand Cup (Asia's oldest football tournament, started 1888) and the Federation Cup are the other major domestic competitions.

 

• India's best performance in international football was the fourth place at the 1956 Melbourne Olympics, and the country won the Asian Games gold in 1951 and 1962.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1), Services (Option 2) and Karnataka (Option 4) have all won the Santosh Trophy in the past, but none of them was the 2024-25 champion. Services won the title in 2023-24 and Karnataka in 2021-22.

question: 'Heart Lamp', the first short-story collection and the first Kannada work to win the International Booker Prize (2025), was written by whom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Banu Mushtaq.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Heart Lamp', written in Kannada by Banu Mushtaq and translated into English by Deepa Bhasthi, won the International Booker Prize 2025, announced at Tate Modern, London, on 20 May 2025. (हार्ट लैंप — बानू मुश्ताक)

 

• The book made history on three counts: it is the first short-story collection ever to win the prize, the first book translated from Kannada to do so, and Deepa Bhasthi became the first Indian translator to win it.

 

• The collection contains 12 stories written between 1990 and 2023 and portrays the lives of Muslim women in small-town and rural southern India. Banu Mushtaq is also a lawyer and activist associated with the Bandaya (protest) literary movement of Karnataka.

 

• The International Booker Prize carries £50,000, shared equally between the author and the translator.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The International Booker Prize is awarded annually for a book translated into English and published in the UK or Ireland; it is distinct from the Booker Prize, which is for original English-language fiction.

 

• The Jnanpith Award, instituted in 1961, is India's highest literary honour; the Sahitya Akademi Award is given annually in 24 recognised languages.

 

NOTE

 

• Geetanjali Shree (Option 2): She won the International Booker Prize in 2022 for 'Tomb of Sand' (Hindi: *Ret Samadhi*), translated by Daisy Rockwell — the first Hindi work to win.

 

• Vivek Shanbhag (Option 3): A Kannada writer, best known for the novel 'Ghachar Ghochar'.

 

• Perumal Murugan (Option 4): A Tamil writer whose novel 'Pyre' (*Pookkuzhi*), translated by Aniruddhan Vasudevan, was longlisted for the International Booker Prize in 2023.

question:
Consider the following statements about landforms produced by wind action:

Statement 1: Barchans are crescent-shaped sand dunes whose horns point in the direction towards which the wind blows.

Statement 2: Loess is a deposit of fine silt laid down by running water in humid regions.

Which of the following Statements is/are Correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. A barchan is a crescent-shaped or moon-shaped sand dune that forms where sand supply is limited and the wind blows steadily from one direction. Its windward slope is gentle and convex, its leeward slope is steep, and its two horns (wings) point downwind, that is, in the direction the wind is moving. (बरखान — अर्धचंद्राकार बालुका स्तूप)

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect. Loess is a deposit of fine, wind-blown (aeolian) silt, not a deposit of running water. It is picked up from deserts and glacial outwash plains and dropped far away. The most extensive loess deposits are in northern China, where the Loess Plateau gives the Hwang Ho (Yellow River) its colour and its name.

 

• Other landforms of wind erosion in deserts include mushroom rocks (gara), yardangs, zeugen, ventifacts, deflation hollows and inselbergs; landforms of wind deposition include barchans, seif (longitudinal) dunes, transverse dunes and loess.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Seif dunes are long, narrow ridges of sand lying parallel to the direction of the wind, whereas transverse dunes lie at right angles to it.

 

• In India, wind-formed landforms are best seen in the Thar Desert of Rajasthan.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are incorrect: Statement 1 is factually accurate and Statement 2 is not, because loess is an aeolian (wind-laid) deposit.

question: Vyommitra, developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), is best described as which of the following?
option_1: A reusable launch vehicle technology demonstrator
option_2: The indigenous cryogenic engine of the LVM3 rocket
option_3: The first module of India's proposed space station
option_4: A half-humanoid robot to be flown on the uncrewed Gaganyaan missions
solution_text:
The correct answer is A half-humanoid robot to be flown on the uncrewed Gaganyaan missions.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vyommitra — from the Sanskrit words *vyoma* (space) and *mitra* (friend) — is a female-looking half-humanoid robot built by ISRO to fly aboard the uncrewed test flights of the Gaganyaan programme before Indian astronauts are sent to space. (व्योममित्र — इसरो का अर्ध-मानवाकार रोबोट)

 

• Its purpose is to simulate the functions of a human crew member: it can read instrument panels, respond to queries from ground control, and operate switches inside the crew module. This validates the Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS), which maintains cabin oxygen, temperature and pressure.

 

• Gaganyaan is India's first human spaceflight programme. The crew module is to be launched by the Human-Rated LVM3 (HLVM3) rocket into a Low Earth Orbit of about 400 km, from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.

 

• The four astronaut-designates announced for Gaganyaan are Group Captains Prashanth Balakrishnan Nair, Ajit Krishnan, Angad Pratap and Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Key Gaganyaan milestones already completed include the Pad Abort Test (2018), the TV-D1 in-flight abort demonstration of the Crew Escape System (October 2023) and successive tests of the parachute and service module propulsion systems.

 

• ISRO was founded in 1969 and is headquartered at Bengaluru. Its founding father is Dr. Vikram Sarabhai.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: ISRO's reusable launch vehicle demonstrator is the RLV-TD ("Pushpak"), which completed a series of autonomous landing experiments.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: The indigenous cryogenic upper-stage engine of LVM3 is the CE-20.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: India's planned space station is the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS), whose first module is targeted for later in this decade.

question:
Which of the following statements about Justice Surya Kant is/are true?

1. He is the 53rd Chief Justice of India.

2. He succeeded Justice B.R. Gavai as the Chief Justice of India.

3. He took oath as the Chief Justice of India in November 2025.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3 all are true.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All three statements are correct. Justice Surya Kant took oath as the 53rd Chief Justice of India on 24 November 2025, administered by President Droupadi Murmu. (न्यायमूर्ति सूर्य कांत — भारत के 53वें मुख्य न्यायाधीश)

 

• He succeeded Justice B.R. Gavai, the 52nd CJI, who held office from 14 May 2025 to 23 November 2025. Justice Gavai was the second Dalit CJI of India, after Justice K.G. Balakrishnan.

 

• Justice Surya Kant was born on 10 February 1962. Before elevation to the Supreme Court in 2019, he served as the Advocate General of Haryana and as the Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court. His tenure as CJI runs until February 2027.

 

• Under Article 124 of the Constitution, the Chief Justice of India is appointed by the President, and by convention the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is elevated. A Supreme Court judge holds office until the age of 65 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Justice H.J. Kania was the first Chief Justice of India, and Justice Y.V. Chandrachud had the longest tenure (about 7 years). Justice K.M. Joseph and others notwithstanding, Justice Fathima Beevi was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court (1989).

 

• The collegium system for judicial appointments evolved through the Three Judges Cases; the 99th Constitutional Amendment and the NJAC Act were struck down by the Supreme Court in 2015.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 are incorrect because each of them omits one statement that is factually correct.

question:
Which of the following are features of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020?

1. It replaces the 10+2 school structure with a 5+3+3+4 curricular design.

2. It recommends raising public investment in education to 6 per cent of GDP.

3. It makes English the compulsory medium of instruction up to Class 5.

4. It proposes a single overarching regulator for higher education, excluding medical and legal education.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1, 2 and 4 are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Education Policy 2020 was approved by the Union Cabinet on 29 July 2020, replacing the National Policy on Education of 1986 (modified 1992). It was drafted by a committee chaired by Dr. K. Kasturirangan. (राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति 2020)

 

• Statement 1 is correct: NEP 2020 replaces the old 10+2 structure with a 5+3+3+4 design — Foundational (ages 3-8), Preparatory (8-11), Middle (11-14) and Secondary (14-18) stages — thereby bringing children aged 3 to 6 within the formal school curriculum for the first time.

 

• Statement 2 is correct: The policy reiterates the target of raising public investment in education to 6 per cent of GDP, a goal first set by the Kothari Commission (1964-66).

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: NEP 2020 states that, wherever possible, the medium of instruction until at least Grade 5, and preferably till Grade 8 and beyond, should be the home language, mother tongue, local language or regional language — not English.

 

• Statement 4 is correct: The policy proposes the Higher Education Commission of India (HECI) as a single umbrella regulator for higher education, excluding medical and legal education, with four verticals for regulation, accreditation, funding and academic standard-setting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other NEP 2020 features: an Academic Bank of Credit, multiple entry and exit in undergraduate programmes, a 4-year multidisciplinary bachelor's degree, the National Testing Agency's common entrance test, and the target of achieving universal foundational literacy and numeracy through the NIPUN Bharat Mission.

 

• The subject of Education lies in the Concurrent List, having been moved there from the State List by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 are incorrect because Statement 3 is factually wrong — NEP 2020 promotes the mother tongue or regional language, not English, as the medium of instruction in early schooling.

question: Glycolysis, the first stage of cellular respiration, takes place in which part of the cell?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The cytoplasm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Glycolysis (from *glykys*, sweet, and *lysis*, splitting) is the breakdown of one molecule of glucose (6 carbon) into two molecules of pyruvate (3 carbon), and it occurs in the cytoplasm of the cell. (ग्लाइकोलाइसिस — कोशिकाद्रव्य में)

 

• Glycolysis is common to both aerobic and anaerobic respiration and does not require oxygen. It yields a net gain of 2 ATP and 2 molecules of NADH per glucose molecule. It is also called the Embden-Meyerhof-Parnas (EMP) pathway.

 

• The later stages of aerobic respiration occur in the mitochondria: the Krebs cycle (citric acid cycle) in the mitochondrial matrix, and the electron transport chain on the inner mitochondrial membrane, where the bulk of the ATP is produced.

 

• The complete aerobic oxidation of one glucose molecule yields about 36 to 38 ATP.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The mitochondrion is called the "powerhouse of the cell" because it generates most of the ATP. It has a double membrane, the inner one folded into cristae, and possesses its own DNA and ribosomes, which is why it is regarded as a semi-autonomous organelle.

 

• ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is called the "energy currency of the cell".

 

NOTE

 

• The mitochondrial matrix (Option 1): The site of the Krebs cycle, not glycolysis.

 

• The inner mitochondrial membrane (Option 3): The site of the electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation.

 

• The nucleus (Option 4): Contains the genetic material and controls cell activities; respiration does not occur here.

question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:

a. Formation of the States Reorganisation Commission under Fazl Ali

b. Creation of Andhra State

c. Appointment of the Dhar Commission on linguistic provinces
solution_text:
The correct answer is c-b-a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct chronological sequence is c - b - a. (राज्य पुनर्गठन — कालानुक्रम)

 

• (c) The Dhar Commission, 1948: The Linguistic Provinces Commission, headed by S.K. Dhar, was appointed in June 1948. It rejected language as the basis for reorganising states and recommended administrative convenience instead. The JVP Committee (1949) — Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya — also rejected the linguistic principle.

 

• (b) Creation of Andhra State, 1953: Following the death of Potti Sriramulu after a 56-day fast, Andhra was carved out of Madras State on 1 October 1953, becoming the first state formed on a linguistic basis.

 

• (a) States Reorganisation Commission, 1953: Set up in December 1953 under the chairmanship of Fazl Ali, with K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru as members. Its 1955 report broadly accepted language as the basis of reorganisation, leading to the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, which created 14 states and 6 union territories.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Later states created include Maharashtra and Gujarat (1960), Nagaland (1963), Haryana (1966), Sikkim (1975), Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand (2000) and Telangana (2014, the 29th state).

 

• Article 3 of the Constitution empowers Parliament to form new states and alter the areas, boundaries or names of existing states.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because the Dhar Commission (1948) came first, the creation of Andhra State (October 1953) came next, and the States Reorganisation Commission (December 1953) came last.

question: Which of the following most accurately describes the Right to Education under Article 21A of the Indian Constitution?
option_1: It is a Directive Principle of State Policy that is enforceable only against the Union Government.
option_2: It is a Fundamental Right guaranteeing free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years.
option_3: It is a Fundamental Duty imposed on parents and guardians alone.
option_4: It is a Fundamental Right guaranteeing free higher education to every citizen up to the age of twenty-one years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is a Fundamental Right guaranteeing free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 21A provides that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may by law determine. (अनुच्छेद 21A — शिक्षा का अधिकार)

 

• It was inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, which made education a Fundamental Right under Part III. The Amendment did three things together:

◦ inserted Article 21A (Fundamental Right to education, 6-14 years)

◦ amended Article 45 (Directive Principle, now early childhood care and education for children below six years)

◦ inserted Article 51A(k) (Fundamental Duty of a parent or guardian to provide education to his child or ward aged 6 to 14 years)

 

• Article 21A was given effect by the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, which came into force on 1 April 2010. The Act reserves 25 per cent of seats in private unaided schools for children from disadvantaged groups and prohibits the detention of a child up to elementary level (later relaxed by a 2019 amendment).

 

• The Supreme Court had earlier read the right to education into Article 21 in Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1993).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 21 guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty and has been judicially expanded to include the right to privacy (K.S. Puttaswamy, 2017), a clean environment, livelihood, health and shelter.

 

• Article 45 originally directed the State to provide free and compulsory education for all children until they completed the age of 14, within ten years of the commencement of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Article 21A is a Fundamental Right in Part III, not a Directive Principle; Directive Principles are non-justiciable.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: The Fundamental Duty of a parent is separately provided under Article 51A(k); Article 21A places the obligation on the State.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: The guarantee covers elementary education for ages 6 to 14, not higher education up to 21 years.

question: In rotational motion, the physical quantity that plays a role analogous to that of mass in linear motion is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Moment of inertia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Moment of inertia (I) is the rotational analogue of mass. Just as mass measures a body's resistance to a change in its linear motion, the moment of inertia measures its resistance to a change in its rotational motion. (जड़त्व आघूर्ण — घूर्णन गति में द्रव्यमान के तुल्य)

 

• For a point mass, I = mr², where *r* is the perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation. Its SI unit is kg m² and it is a scalar quantity. Unlike mass, it is not a fixed property of a body: it depends on the distribution of mass about the chosen axis.

 

• The linear and rotational analogues are:

◦ Mass (m) — Moment of inertia (I)

◦ Force (F) — Torque (τ = Iα)

◦ Linear velocity (v) — Angular velocity (ω)

◦ Linear momentum (p = mv) — Angular momentum (L = Iω)

◦ Linear acceleration (a) — Angular acceleration (α)

◦ Kinetic energy (½mv²) — Rotational kinetic energy (½Iω²)

 

• A common illustration is a spinning skater: when the skater pulls the arms inward, the moment of inertia decreases and, since angular momentum is conserved, the angular velocity increases.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The law of conservation of angular momentum states that in the absence of an external torque, Iω remains constant.

 

• Moment of inertia of a solid sphere about a diameter is (2/5)MR², of a thin ring about its central axis MR², and of a solid disc about its central axis ½MR².

 

NOTE

 

• Torque (Option 1): The rotational analogue of force; τ = r × F, measured in newton metre.

 

• Angular momentum (Option 2): The rotational analogue of linear momentum; L = Iω, measured in kg m² s⁻¹.

 

• Angular velocity (Option 4): The rotational analogue of linear velocity; it is the same for every particle of a rigid body about a given axis.

question: Among the three new criminal laws that came into force on 1 July 2024, which one replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Three new criminal laws came into force on 1 July 2024, replacing colonial-era statutes. (तीन नए आपराधिक कानून — 1 जुलाई 2024)

◦ Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860

◦ Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973

◦ Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023 replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872

 

• The BNSS deals with procedure — arrest, investigation, bail, trial, appeals and sentencing. It contains 531 sections, against 484 in the old CrPC.

 

• Notable BNSS provisions include Zero FIR (an FIR can be registered at any police station irrespective of jurisdiction), e-FIR and electronic filing, videography of search and seizure, mandatory forensic investigation for offences punishable with seven years or more, and time limits — for example, judgment must be delivered within 45 days of the completion of trial and charges framed within 60 days of the first hearing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The BNS has 358 sections and introduces community service as a punishment, a specific offence of organised crime and of terrorism, and snatching; sedition (old Section 124A) has been replaced by an offence relating to acts endangering the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.

 

• The BSA gives electronic and digital records the status of primary evidence.

 

• Criminal law, criminal procedure and evidence are all subjects of the Concurrent List.

 

NOTE

 

• The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (Option 1): Replaced the substantive criminal law, the IPC 1860.

 

• The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (Option 3): Replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: There is no enactment called the "Bharatiya Dand Sanhita, 2023"; *Bharatiya Dand Sanhita* was simply the Hindi name of the old Indian Penal Code.

question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct option:

Assertion (A): Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY provides a health cover of Rs. 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation.

Reason (R): PM-JAY is the world's largest government-funded health assurance scheme.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), launched on 23 September 2018 from Ranchi, Jharkhand, provides a health cover of Rs. 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation. (आयुष्मान भारत — प्रधानमंत्री जन आरोग्य योजना)

 

• Reason (R) is true. PM-JAY is described as the world's largest government-funded health assurance scheme, covering about 12 crore poor and vulnerable families (roughly 55 crore beneficiaries), identified on the basis of the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011.

 

• However, R is not the explanation of A. The size of the scheme's beneficiary base is what makes it the largest in the world; it is not the reason why the cover was fixed at Rs. 5 lakh. The two statements state separate facts about the same scheme.

 

• Key features of PM-JAY: it is completely cashless and paperless at empanelled hospitals, is portable across the country, has no cap on family size, age or gender, and covers pre-existing diseases from day one, along with 3 days of pre-hospitalisation and 15 days of post-hospitalisation expenses. The implementing agency is the National Health Authority (NHA).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ayushman Bharat has two components: PM-JAY (the insurance arm) and Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (formerly Health and Wellness Centres), which deliver comprehensive primary healthcare.

 

• Under Ayushman Vay Vandana, launched in 2024, all citizens aged 70 years and above are eligible for the Rs. 5 lakh cover irrespective of income.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Although both statements are true, R does not explain why A is so.

 

• Options 3 and 4 are incorrect: Both the Assertion and the Reason are factually correct.

question: Ghoomar, a traditional folk dance performed by women who move in circles in flowing ghagharas, is associated with which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ghoomar is the best-known folk dance of Rajasthan. Its name comes from *ghoomna*, meaning to whirl or pirouette, describing the graceful circular movement of the dancers. (घूमर — राजस्थान का लोक नृत्य)

 

• It is traditionally performed by women dressed in long, flowing ghagharas, and was originally associated with the Bhil community before being adopted by the royal households of Rajputana. It is performed on festive occasions such as Teej, Gangaur and Holi, and by a new bride on entering her marital home.

 

• Other important folk dances of Rajasthan include Kalbeliya (of the Kalbeliya snake-charmer community, inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010), Kachhi Ghodi, Bhavai, Chari, Terah Taali and Gair.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Some other well-known state folk dances:

◦ Gujarat — Garba, Dandiya Raas, Bhavai, Tippani

◦ Punjab — Bhangra, Giddha

◦ Assam — Bihu

◦ Maharashtra — Lavani, Tamasha

◦ Jammu & Kashmir — Rouf, Dumhal

◦ Himachal Pradesh — Nati

◦ Uttarakhand — Chholiya, Jhora

◦ Chhattisgarh — Panthi, Raut Nacha

 

• India's eight classical dances are Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): Known for Garba and Dandiya Raas, performed chiefly during Navratri.

 

• Haryana (Option 3): Known for Khoria, Dhamal and Phag dances.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 4): Known for Matki, Grida, Karma and Charkula dances.

question: According to the Global Firepower Military Strength Ranking 2026, India occupies which position among the countries assessed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Global Firepower (GFP) Military Strength Ranking 2026, India is placed 4th out of 145 countries assessed, with a PowerIndex (PwrIndx) score of about 0.1346. India retained the same rank as in 2025. (ग्लोबल फायरपावर 2026 — भारत चौथे स्थान पर)

 

• The top three positions are held by the United States (1st), Russia (2nd) and China (3rd).

 

• A lower PowerIndex score indicates greater military strength; a hypothetical "perfect" score is 0.0000.

 

• The GFP index is compiled from over 60 individual factors, including manpower, equipment holdings across land, air and naval forces, financial position (defence budget), logistical capability, natural resources and geography. Nuclear stockpiles are not counted directly, though recognised nuclear powers receive a bonus.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India is the world's most populous country and maintains one of the largest standing armies. The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) post was created in 2019, and the first CDS was General Bipin Rawat.

 

• Defence-related indices and reports to remember: the SIPRI Yearbook (Stockholm International Peace Research Institute) on arms transfers and military expenditure, and the Military Balance published by the IISS, London.

 

NOTE

 

• 2nd (Option 1) is held by Russia, and 3rd (Option 2) by China in the 2026 ranking.

 

• 6th (Option 4) is incorrect; India has consistently featured in the top five of the Global Firepower ranking in recent years.

question: On the basis of ownership, an industry that is jointly owned and run by the State and by individuals or a group of individuals is classified as which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is A joint sector industry.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On the basis of ownership, industries are classified into four categories. (स्वामित्व के आधार पर उद्योगों का वर्गीकरण)

◦ Public sector — owned and operated by government agencies, e.g. BHEL, SAIL, ONGC

◦ Private sector — owned and operated by individuals or a group of individuals, e.g. TISCO, Bajaj Auto, Reliance Industries

◦ Joint sector — jointly run by the State and individuals or a group of individuals, e.g. Oil India Limited (OIL), Maruti Udyog in its earlier form

◦ Cooperative sector — owned and operated by the producers or suppliers of raw materials, the workers, or both, who pool resources and share profits and losses proportionately, e.g. Amul (Anand Milk Union Limited), the sugar industry of Maharashtra, the coir industry of Kerala

 

• Industries are also classified by:

◦ Raw material — agro-based, mineral-based, marine-based, forest-based

◦ Size (capital and labour employed) — small scale, large scale

◦ Bulk and weight of raw material and finished goods — heavy industries (iron and steel), light industries (electronics)

◦ Role — basic or key industries (iron and steel, copper smelting) and consumer industries (toothpaste, sugar, paper)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Amul is the classic Indian example of the cooperative model; it grew out of the Kaira District Co-operative Milk Producers' Union and led to Operation Flood, the White Revolution, under Dr. Verghese Kurien.

 

• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 classified industries into three schedules and formed the basis of the public-sector-led model, which was substantially liberalised by the New Industrial Policy of 1991.

 

NOTE

 

• A public sector industry (Option 1): Owned and managed wholly by government agencies, not jointly with private individuals.

 

• A private sector industry (Option 2): Owned by a single individual or a group of individuals, with no State participation.

 

• A cooperative sector industry (Option 4): Owned by the producers, suppliers or workers themselves, who share the profits and losses; the State is not a co-owner in the manner of the joint sector.

question: Which of the following subjects was NOT transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Public order.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, often called the "Mini-Constitution", transferred five subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List. (42वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1976)

◦ Education

◦ Forests

◦ Weights and measures

◦ Protection of wild animals and birds

◦ Administration of justice; constitution and organisation of all courts except the Supreme Court and the High Courts

 

• Public order was not among them. Public order (Entry 1) and Police (Entry 2) remain in the State List, and are the two entries that head that list.

 

• Other important changes made by the 42nd Amendment: it added the words Socialist, Secular and Integrity to the Preamble, added Part IVA (Fundamental Duties, Article 51A) on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, added Part IVB (Article 31D), provided for Administrative Tribunals (Part XIV-A), and made the President bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers.

 

• The Seventh Schedule contains three lists: Union List (List I), State List (List II) and Concurrent List (List III). In case of a conflict over a Concurrent List subject, Union law prevails (Article 254).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Many of the excesses of the 42nd Amendment were reversed by the 43rd and 44th Amendment Acts (1977 and 1978), enacted by the Janata Government. The 44th Amendment removed the Right to Property from Fundamental Rights and placed it under Article 300A.

 

• The idea of three lists in the Seventh Schedule was borrowed from the Government of India Act, 1935.

 

NOTE

 

• Education (Option 1), Forests (Option 2) and Weights and measures (Option 3) were all shifted from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment, and therefore cannot be the answer to a question asking which was NOT transferred.

question: The 30th Conference of the Parties (COP30) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change was held in November 2025 in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Belem, Brazil.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• COP30 was held from 10 to 21 November 2025 at Belem, a city in the Amazon region of Brazil. The Brazilian presidency branded it the "COP of implementation", with the emphasis on turning past pledges into action. (सीओपी30 — बेलेम, ब्राज़ील)

 

• Key outcomes of COP30 included a call to mobilise USD 1.3 trillion a year by 2035 for climate action in developing countries, an agreement to triple adaptation finance by 2035, the operationalisation of replenishment cycles for the Loss and Damage Fund, and the launch of the Global Implementation Accelerator and the Belem Mission to 1.5°C.

 

• A notable gap was the absence of an explicit roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels in the final decision text.

 

• The UNFCCC was adopted at the Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro in 1992 and entered into force in 1994. The first COP was held at Berlin in 1995.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Recent and forthcoming COPs: COP26 Glasgow (2021), COP27 Sharm el-Sheikh (2022), COP28 Dubai (2023), COP29 Baku (2024), COP30 Belem (2025), COP31 Antalya, Turkiye (2026) and COP32 Addis Ababa, Ethiopia (2027) — the first COP to be hosted by a least-developed country.

 

• The Paris Agreement was adopted at COP21 (2015) and aims to hold the rise in global average temperature to well below 2°C, and preferably to 1.5°C, above pre-industrial levels. India's announced targets include net zero by 2070 and 500 GW of non-fossil-fuel energy capacity by 2030.

 

NOTE

 

• Baku, Azerbaijan (Option 1): Hosted COP29 in 2024, known for the New Collective Quantified Goal on climate finance.

 

• Dubai, UAE (Option 2): Hosted COP28 in 2023, which concluded the first Global Stocktake and operationalised the Loss and Damage Fund.

 

• Antalya, Turkiye (Option 3): Will host COP31 in 2026, with Australia serving as president of negotiations.

question: Radiocarbon dating, used to estimate the age of ancient organic remains such as wood, bone and cloth, is based on the radioactive decay of which isotope?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carbon-14.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Radiocarbon dating measures the residual amount of the radioactive isotope carbon-14 (¹⁴C) in material that was once living. (रेडियोकार्बन डेटिंग — कार्बन-14)

 

• Carbon-14 is continuously produced in the upper atmosphere when cosmic-ray neutrons strike nitrogen-14 atoms. Living organisms absorb it along with ordinary carbon; when the organism dies, intake stops and the ¹⁴C already present begins to decay by beta emission back into nitrogen-14.

 

• The half-life of carbon-14 is about 5,730 years, which makes the method useful for dating specimens up to roughly 50,000 years old. The technique was developed by Willard Libby, who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1960 for it.

 

• Carbon has three important isotopes — C-12 (the standard for atomic mass, stable), C-13 (stable) and C-14 (radioactive). Isotopes are atoms of the same element having the same atomic number but different mass numbers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Radioactivity was discovered by Henri Becquerel (1896); Marie and Pierre Curie discovered polonium and radium. Radioactive emissions are of three kinds — alpha (helium nuclei), beta (electrons) and gamma (electromagnetic radiation).

 

• Other applications of radioisotopes: cobalt-60 in cancer therapy, iodine-131 for thyroid disorders, sodium-24 to trace blood circulation, and phosphorus-32 in agricultural research.

 

NOTE

 

• Potassium-40 (Option 2): Used in potassium-argon dating of rocks and minerals; its half-life is about 1.25 billion years, and its decay is the source of most of the argon in the Earth's atmosphere.

 

• Uranium-238 (Option 3): Used in uranium-lead dating of very old rocks; half-life about 4.5 billion years.

 

• Rubidium-87 (Option 4): Used in rubidium-strontium dating, again for extremely old geological samples, not organic remains.

question: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in which Part of the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part IV.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs) are contained in Part IV of the Constitution, in Articles 36 to 51. (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व — भाग IV, अनुच्छेद 36-51)

 

• The idea of DPSPs was borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland, which in turn had taken it from Spain. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described them as "novel features" of the Indian Constitution, and they have been called the "conscience of the Constitution" by Granville Austin.

 

• Article 37 expressly provides that the Directive Principles are not enforceable by any court, but that they are nevertheless fundamental in the governance of the country and it is the duty of the State to apply them in making laws. They are therefore non-justiciable, unlike Fundamental Rights (Part III, Articles 12-35), which are enforceable through the courts under Articles 32 and 226.

 

• Important Directive Principles include Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), Article 40 (organisation of village panchayats), Article 44 (uniform civil code), Article 45 (early childhood care and education), Article 47 (raising the level of nutrition and prohibition of intoxicating drinks) and Article 51 (promotion of international peace and security).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The relationship between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs was settled by the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) and the Minerva Mills case (1980), in which the Supreme Court held that harmony and balance between the two is part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

 

• Article 31C, inserted by the 25th Amendment, protects laws made to implement the Directive Principles in Articles 39(b) and 39(c) from challenge under Articles 14 and 19.

 

NOTE

 

• Part III (Option 1): Contains the Fundamental Rights (Articles 12 to 35).

 

• Part IVA (Option 3): Contains the Fundamental Duties under Article 51A, added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.

 

• Part V (Option 4): Deals with the Union — the President, Vice-President, Council of Ministers, Parliament and the Supreme Court.
